title: A diagram of positive height has a defect region
statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If $h(D)>0$, then the Seifert picture $S$ of $D$ contains a defect region, i.e. a component of $S^2\setminus S$ supporting a reducing arc joining an incoherent pair of Seifert circles.
strategy: Each complementary region $R$ has genus zero with $k\ge1$ boundary circles; classify the exposed circles of $R$: one exposed circle gives no pair, two exposed circles give either a disk (with a signed arc, hence coherent circles) or an annulus (a defect region exactly when the two are incoherent), and three or more exposed circles always contain an incoherent pair. Suppose no region is a defect region; then every region is one of the non-defect types, and at least one region lies between two nested coherent circles joined by a signed arc (otherwise $h=0$). Trying to build a picture with no defect regions from such a region, the only possible additions are coherent circles nested with the given ones, producing again height zero; contradiction. This is the survey's Lemma 2.2 in full. The region classification consumes the annulus lemma and the coherence relation, so the statement is made under AC; the finite case analysis of exposed circles uses no further choice.

references.title: Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
